title: Luminescence Resonance Energy Transfer to Study Conformational Changes in Membrane Proteins Expressed in Mammalian Cells
protocol: Clone the gene expressing the protein of interest into a suitable vector.
Choose labeling sites on the protein that can reflect possible conformational changes.
Use crystal structures or homologous proteins to determine appropriate labeling sites if available.
Predict the structure of the protein using online software if no crystal structure is available.
Select residues with surface-exposed and accessible side chains for fluorophore tagging.
Choose residues that are not critical to protein function, such as those not involved in ligand binding.
Introduce cysteine mutations at preferred sites similar to existing residues to minimize perturbation.
Make mutations to ensure that the protein only gives LRET from intended sites using standard site-directed mutagenesis protocols.
Mutate away non-disulfide-bonded cysteines that could potentially bind to maleimide-conjugated fluorescent tags.
Introduce cysteine residues in desired sites by making point mutations using standard site-directed mutagenesis protocols.
Include a protease cleavage site near the introduced cysteine, such as LVPRGS or IEGR sequences, accessible to protease cleavage.
Choose the site such that upon cleavage one of the introduced cysteines dissociates from the rest of the protein.
Perform a western blot to confirm expression of the mutated protein.
Perform a functional assay of the protein to ensure minimal alteration in function due to mutations.
Select fluorophores based on the expected distance range being measured, typically between 0.5-1x the R0 of the fluorophore pair.
Transiently transfect the protein of interest into chosen mammalian cells using common transfection reagents.
Use four 10-cm dishes per LRET experiment for HEK and CHO cell lines.
Allow the cells to express the protein for 36-48 hours before harvesting.
Detach HEK cells by pipetting buffer against the bottom of the dish.
Detach CHO cells using a cell scraper, washing off the media with extracellular buffer.
Collect detached cells by centrifuging at 1,100 x g for 3 min.
Suspend collected cells in 3 ml of extracellular buffer.
Add donor and acceptor fluorophores in equimolar amounts to achieve a final concentration of 100-300 nM.
Incubate the suspension on a rotator for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash labeled cells 3-4 times with extracellular buffer to remove unbound fluorophores.
Suspend washed cells in 2 ml of extracellular buffer for LRET measurements.
Label a separate set of cells with only donor fluorophore (terbium chelate) without adding any acceptor fluorophore.
Place resuspended cells in a quartz cuvette with at least 1 ml volume.
Turn on the computer.
Turn on the instrument.
Adjust the parameters of the data acquisition program accordingly.
Set the excitation wavelength to the absorbance range of the donor fluorophore (330-340 nm).
Set the emission wavelength appropriately for the acceptor used.
Select a detection wavelength that measures only the acceptor emission and does not include bleed-through from the donor’s emission.
Use a wavelength of 565 nm for Alexa 555 as an acceptor.
For donor-only measurements, use a wavelength of 545 nm for measuring terbium chelate emission.
Set the length of emission detection to be at least three times the expected LRET lifetime.
Perform the scan.
Do at least three scans of 99 sweeps to ensure consistency of results.
Save the results as a text file (*.txt).
Alter the conditions to measure conformational changes of the protein.
Add glutamate to 1 mM to the same sample scanned previously.
Scan again after altering the conditions.
Add up to five units of the appropriate protease to the sample.
Take scans continually until cleavage is complete and no further change is seen in the lifetime for three successive scans.
If a Factor Xa cleavage site is being used, add 3 μl of Factor Xa to the sample.
Scan every 30 min for 3 hr if using Factor Xa.
Open the data analysis software.
Load the fluorescence lifetime data by using Import ASCII to open the text files.
Load all the replicates as well as the final background measurements into one file.
Highlight the columns that contain the individual trials.
Under the Data menu in the menu bar, click on Statistics on Rows to display the average fluorescence intensities from the trials, as well as the standard deviation and standard error.

Plot the average values as a line graph with fluorescence intensity on the Y-axis and lifetime in microseconds on the X-axis to create a curve that represents the lifetime of the sensitized emission of the acceptor.
Change the Y-axis of the plot to a log scale for better visualization of the data.
Repeat step 8.3 on the background measurement data, averaging the final scans that show overlap indicating complete cleavage.
Display the mean background data on the same plot as the averaged raw data.
Open the Layer Control dialog box from the Plot menu.
Transfer the background mean data into the list of Layer Contents.
Align the mean background data to the mean raw data using the Simple Math function.
Multiply or divide the background data until its tail end overlaps with that of the raw data.
Subtract the aligned background signal from the initial raw LRET signal using the Simple Math function.
Fit the data to an exponential decay curve using the Select Fitting Function dialog box.
Set the start boundary for fitting after the end of the laser pulse.
Use the same startpoint for all subsequent curve fittings.
Fit the fluorescence data using a single exponential decay function with x0 fixed to 0.
Determine the goodness of fit by analyzing the residual.
Calculate the distance between fluorophores using the Förster equation based on measured τDA.
Repeat the experiment and data analysis at least three times for reproducibility.
Use additional control experiments or repetitions if there is inconsistency in individual measurements.
Calculate errors in measurement using a suitable error analysis calculator.
